cards.text: Meet Absalom, King David's son (2 Samuel 3:3). The king has just summoned him and kissed him (2 Samuel 14:33), and some time later, Absalom gets himself a chariot with horses, plus a little extra. Me? Years in a junk drawer, and the fanciest ride I ever got was sliding to the back every time somebody slammed it shut.

cards.question: Besides a chariot and horses, what else does Absalom provide for himself?

answers.text: Fifty men to run ahead of him
Four hundred men to go up with him
Six hundred men to march with him

cards.text: Absalom gets up EARLY to stand beside the road leading to the city gate and call out to anyone bringing a grievance for the king to decide. Friend, my oven timer has to go off three times before I even roll over.

cards.question: When Absalom calls out to someone bringing a grievance to the king, he asks what city the person is from.

cards.text: Say the man answers that he's from one of the tribes of Israel. That's when Absalom leans in.

cards.question: Absalom tells the man from one of the tribes of Israel that his claims are weak.
Absalom tells a man bringing a grievance to the king that his claims are good and right. So what does Absalom say the problem is?

answers.text: The king has no deputy to hear him
The king's judges have been bribed
The king is busy fighting a war

cards.text: Then Absalom adds a wish. If only someone would give him a certain job, he says, everyone with a grievance or dispute could come to him, and he would give each one justice.

cards.question: Absalom says he wishes someone would appoint him ___ in the land.

cards.text: And it's not just talk. When people come close to bow down to him, Absalom has a move ready for that too.

cards.question: What does Absalom do when someone approaches to bow down to him?

answers.text: Takes hold of him and kisses him
Lets him bow and walks away
Has his runners push him back

cards.text: Absalom does this to ALL the Israelites who come to the king for justice. This man is shaking more hands than a greeter at the church door on Easter Sunday.

cards.question: By meeting people on the road to the gate, talking up their claims and kissing them, Absalom stole the ___ of the men of Israel.

cards.text: After four years pass, Absalom asks the king to let him go to Hebron to fulfill a vow he made to the LORD. He says he promised to worship the LORD in Hebron if the LORD brought him back to Jerusalem.

cards.question: Absalom says he made his vow to worship the LORD in Hebron while he was living somewhere else. Where?
When Absalom asks to go to Hebron to fulfill his vow, King David tells him to go in peace.

cards.text: So Absalom gets up and goes to Hebron, and then he sends spies throughout the tribes of Israel with a message. SPIES, friend, on a worship trip!

cards.question: Absalom's spies carry a message across the tribes of Israel: when you hear the sound of the horn, say something. What is it?

cards.text: Two hundred men from Jerusalem go along with Absalom, invited as guests. Friend, hand me an invitation and I'm hopping out the door, gold base and all, before you finish the sentence.

cards.question: The two hundred guests from Jerusalem know all about Absalom's plan.

cards.text: Then Absalom sends for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, to come from his hometown of Giloh. That's like the other team calling up your own coach at halftime.

cards.question: Absalom sends for David's counselor Ahithophel while he's offering the ___.
As Ahithophel is called in, what happens to Absalom's following?

cards.text: The conspiracy is gaining strength. And that's where we'll pause for now, friend, because this story is FAR from over.
